scene: Day 115, pouring rain, outside the depot wall. Patch (white round head, orange bandage above his right eye, orange backpack) hangs halfway up a wet rope against the grey concrete wall, one foot in a loop, looking back over his shoulder with wide terrified eyes and one sweat drop. Above the top of the wall, a packed yard of green walkers tilts hundreds of faces up toward him, with the canopy and the beige coach behind them. Beside him swings the hand-painted cardboard sign, its yellow paint running in the rain (letters not legible). At the top of the frame, on the gantry, an arm with a purple band and a figure in a red beanie haul on the rope. Tense because one slip drops him into the street and every dead face in the yard is watching him climb.

Day 91, night, a long concrete flyover ramp. The white box truck rolls downhill with its headlights off and its engine silent, Patch's frightened face pressed to the passenger window, orange bandage visible, while the driver beside him is only a dark silhouette with two hands on the wheel. Behind and above them, the top of the flyover is packed rail to rail with green walkers silhouetted against a huge pale moon, the one in the ragged olive-gray vest at the front, all facing the spot where the horn last sounded. Tense because a single noise from the truck would turn the whole bridge around.
